The single player story is pretty good for a fighting game. Only problem is that the difficulty curve is basically non-existent. This unfortunately does not ready many newer fighting game players for online play. On the other hand there is likely to be some enjoyment if they just want to see more Dragon Ball franchise lore first hand. That being said if those same people only want to play multiplayer at home with friends the game mechanics are not so complex that it's totally unintuitive to naturally get better. Both the low and high end of skill progression feels very rewarding. This is definitely in my top 5 fighting games of all time.

I'd have killed to play a game like this back in the 80/90's.

[+] Visually stunning.
[+] Extremely fun to play.
[+] Faithful to the original material with a lot of references.
[+] Finally a good DBZ fighting game.
[+] Majin C21

but...

[-] Story mode is forgettable and boring, if you want C21 in your team, you will have to play (at least) 8 hours of this repetitive crap.
[-] Lobby is confusing in the beginning, they should have kept the room system from GGREV2.
[-] All characters have this kind of same feeling, of course they have different/unique moves and mechanics (sometimes) but they play kinda the same for the most part. There's some depth though, especially with assist management and team synergy.
[-] Lot of things are too easy if you're used to 2D Fighters, autocombos on every button, easy motions (no srk, hcb/f or 360), a parry system with a LOT of active frames, that dragon rush throw thing, homing dash safe on block (you can punish it on reaction with 2H but still...)
They needed to reduce the gap between veterans and newcomers, it's DBZ after all but it's a bit too much. However, If you're new to air dasher, it's a good time to jump in.

Anyway, it's still really enjoyable, simply the best DBZ fighting game you will ever play.

Three things you need to know.

This is the best DBZ game ever made.
This may be the best fighting game ever made.
You will be bad at it and you will not understand why.

I recommended this game only when the full version is on sale (Legendary Edition at the time of reviewing). Since it's owned by Bandai, the monetization is pretty predatory, in this case, locking 2/3 of the roster behind a paywall.

If you can afford or manage to get past that, the game still ages extremely well with animation, faithful modeling, and a fighting system. You can easily feel the care and passion poured into every single character by Arc System Work, one of the highlights in the whole DBZ game franchise. Enjoy the hell out of it despite not being a part of online PVP.

tldr.text: Very Positive (91%): players praise the story and characters most, along with the fighting.
The most common complaint is characters locked behind paywalls, followed by the price.

details.text: Players who had played under 2 hours when reviewing are far less positive, at 70%, than those with 2 to 10 hours, at 92%.
Recent reviews are about as positive as the all-time score, so the overall picture has held steady for buyers now.
